turns.speaker: Steve
turns.text: That's a fascinating aspect of cross-cultural research. In one of my studies on emotions, we encountered difficulties translating the concept of "Schadenfreude" from German to English. Participants in Germany described it as "a little satisfaction when someone gets what's coming to them," which doesn't quite capture the nuances of the word. A participant from Japan mentioned that the closest equivalent to Schadenfreude in their culture is "yutori," but even that doesn't fully convey the emotional complexity of the concept.
